mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns despite falling federal funds rates, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals stronger demand in the housing market, which may boost related industries and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate earnings, driving S&P 500 returns up over 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production (INDPRO) suggests strong supply chains and economic growth, which can positively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the federal funds rate below 1% triggers increased investment and borrowing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS drops below 1% but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is strong and unemployment (UNRATE) is low, consumer confidence and spending increase, driving S&P 500 returns up over 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is strong and unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If inflation rises in a late-cycle expansion but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) alongside job growth (PAYEMS) indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS and PAYEMS increase but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.
